chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: The new Moten band's records and Durham as sole arranger
summary: He says Lafayette, Toby and similar numbers were his, with Barefield contributing, and no one else was writing for the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, you know the first sort of records that Morton made, with that sort of new band, well, the band was still pretty rough then, wasn't it?
Yeah, they had a funny, peculiar sound, due to the tone. They didn't like for it to be changed too much. But it had to be changed.
Well, I mean, you know, those things that you recorded, Lafayette and Toby and all those things --
Yeah, that was the new band.

Lafayette and Toby and all those things. Barefield was with me on Toby. He had created some of the things. And some of the things he played, I wrote them down, because he was a writer, too. All those are my numbers, there.
Well, let me just check now so we get this straight. Did anybody else arrange for the band then?
No, nobody else was doing it. If anybody else was writing, he quit. Nobody wrote anything after I got there.
